extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting contributed-talk abstracts to ASL meetings (logic researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for preparing and submitting abstracts of contributed talks to Association for Symbolic Logic (ASL) meetings, including format, length, authorship, membership, and typesetting/proof procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts that do not conform to these requirements will be returned immediately to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonconforming submissions are not accepted; follow all listed rules to avoid immediate return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts received after the announced deadline will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions are excluded from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASL membership requirement (North America meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ASL meetings in North America (Annual, JMM, APA), at least one author of each contributed abstract must be an ASL member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This membership requirement does not apply to the ASL European Summer Meeting, Asian Logic Conference, or SLALM. Additionally, abstracts are only published in The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic meeting reports if at least one author is a member at the time the report is sent for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship identification and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed author must be an identifiable human being and all persons mentioned as authors must have given their approval for the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The usual rules about authorship for The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic apply to abstracts as well. Ensure every author is real and has consented to being listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals are invited to submit contributed papers for presentation at an ASL meeting that have logic research content that lies within the scope of the interests of the ASL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be on topics and research questions aligned with ASL interests; off-topic abstracts may be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-author submission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals' names may appear as authors or co-authors on up to 3 abstracts per meeting; however, each set of authors may only submit one abstract per meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An author can be on up to three abstracts, but a particular collaboration (same set of authors) can submit only one abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limit (300 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts of contributed talks are limited to 300 words (about three quarters of a page in the standard, 11pt LaTeX article style), including the title, other heading material, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count all text including title, headings, and references toward the 300-word maximum. Keep abstracts concise and within the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and preferred formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting both invited and contributed abstracts must do so via email, preferably as a LaTex or TeX file; however, ASCII and Doc will also be accepted. Authors may also submit via post as a hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting TeX or Word, the file should be fully processed and accompanied by a PDF in which all mathematical symbols are visible and correct for the typeset version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ASL abstract template for TeX submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting abstracts as TeX files, please use the ASL abstract template and associated document class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rename the template using your last name before submitting it as an attachment. Complete instructions on how to use the template are included in ASLabstracttemplate.tex (distributed in the ASL Abstract Templates zip).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each abstract submission must include the complete address of at least one author, including an email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full postal address and an email for correspondence and publication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No drawings or footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts may not include drawings or footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid embedding figures, drawings, or footnotes in the abstract; keep it plain text/math only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete references required
rubrics_metrics.description: The references must be complete: author, title, full name of journal, year, volume, page numbers, and for books, complete publisher data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full bibliographic details for any cited works; incomplete references are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-form submission and typesetting/proof procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Typesetting is done immediately after the submission deadline, so abstracts should be in final form when they are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A typeset booklet of abstracts will be distributed to participants. Galley proofs are given to authors at or before the meeting and must be corrected, approved, and returned immediately after receipt; no changes other than corrections of typesetting errors may be made.
